chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Trummy Young's group at the Three Deuces
summary: A five-to-seven piece band with Trummy Young that lacked promotion and machinery behind it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, we had a nice little outfit on 52nd Street, at the Three Deuces.
How big a group was it?
We had a full rhythm section, Trummy and I forget who was -- who was playing with us in the front line. It was about, you know, five or six or seven pieces, something like that.

But we just couldn't get it -- we did a lot of work, worked at it, and when I was living out in Brooklyn, as I said once before, Trummy would come out to the house and my wife would fix one of those down home breakfasts and all that. You know, we'd sit and eat, I'd eat a dozen biscuits. Then we'd go in the front room and work over some things at the piano, but we just -- you know, you have to have that promotion and the machinery behind the group, no matter what the talent is. You can be -- you can have a million dollars worth of talent, but you have to have that -- the machinery behind you to make a thing come off.
